question.text: A client's Rs. 100 lakh portfolio generated 20% return. Fixed management fee 1.5%, operating expenses 0.5%, performance fee 20% above a 10% hurdle (performance fee = Rs. 1.55 lakh after expenses and fixed fee), and exit load 2%. Net portfolio at year-end (after all fees) is approximately:

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook's worked example: gross value Rs. 120 lakh, less operating expenses Rs. 0.60 lakh, less fixed management fee Rs. 1.65 lakh, less performance fee Rs. 1.55 lakh, less exit load Rs. 2.324 lakh, giving a net value of approximately Rs. 113.88 lakh. The Trap: Rs. 120 lakh ignores all fees and the exit load; Rs. 115 lakh is a back-of-envelope approximation; Rs. 100 lakh wrongly assumes zero net return after fees. Note: Apply the fee waterfall in the same order as the workbook (gross, operating expenses, fixed fee, performance fee, exit load) so that the performance-fee base and exit-load base match the source calculation.
